one_liner: CUDA Huffman decoder (CUHD) that splits one unpartitioned bitstream across GPU threads by self-synchronization; reported 10x+ over zstd's CPU huff0.
what_it_does: Decodes a single raw Huffman-coded byte stream on an NVIDIA GPU without needing block boundaries, gap arrays or other side information in the stream. The API is a C++ class set in namespace cuhd: wrap the compressed 32-bit units and a decoder table in CUHDGPUInputBuffer/CUHDGPUCodetable, allocate CUHDGPUOutputBuffer and CUHDGPUDecoderMemory, then call the static CUHDGPUDecoder::decode(). It ships a basic sequential length-limited Huffman encoder (llhuff) that produces the matching stream and table; it is not a drop-in for zstd/huff0 or deflate streams.
how_it_is_fast: Uses the self-synchronization property of Huffman codes: each thread starts decoding a small subsequence (4 x 32-bit units in the demo) at an arbitrary bit offset, and decoding from a wrong offset usually falls back into codeword alignment within a few codewords. Phase 1 synchronizes subsequences within a thread block, phase 2 is relaunched until every block boundary has synchronized, phase 3 is a Thrust exclusive scan over per-subsequence symbol counts to get output offsets, and phase 4 re-decodes and writes symbols in parallel. Each symbol is decoded by a single direct lookup in a 2^11-entry table using a two-word sliding window.
when_to_use: You control both encoder and decoder and need to decode large (tens of MB and up) byte-symbol Huffman streams that already live on, or are headed to, an NVIDIA GPU.
You cannot afford to add partition metadata (gap arrays, chunk offsets) to the stream format but still want GPU-wide parallel decode.
Research or baseline use: it is the reference self-synchronization GPU Huffman decoder (ICPP 2018) that later work such as ipdps22-opthuffdec builds on and compares against.
Throughput-bound pipelines where amortizing host-to-device transfers and kernel launches over a big buffer is acceptable.
when_not_to_use: Decoding standard formats (deflate, zstd/huff0, JPEG): codeword length is capped at MAX_CODEWORD_LENGTH = 11 (compile-time) and the bit layout is CUHD's own 32-bit-unit format from its llhuff encoder.
Alphabets larger than 256 symbols: SYMBOL_TYPE is std::uint8_t.
Small inputs or latency-sensitive calls: the decode runs four kernel phases, a host round-trip per phase-2 iteration and a Thrust scan, plus PCIe copies.
Codes or data that synchronize slowly: phase 2 is relaunched in a host loop until all sequences synchronize, so the number of passes is data-dependent and unbounded in the code.
Production use that needs a maintained library, AMD/Intel GPUs, Windows or macOS: the README targets GNU/Linux and CUDA only, and there are no commits since 2019-02-02.

integration.dependencies: CUDA runtime and driver (libcudart, libcuda), Thrust (bundled with the CUDA toolkit); the bundled encoder/ subdirectory for encoding
integration.min_toolchain: README: GCC 5.4.0+ and CUDA SDK 8+; the Makefile compiles host code with -std=c++17 -O3 -march=native -Wall -Werror and device code with nvcc --std=c++11 -O3, so a GCC with C++17 support is needed in practice
integration.platforms: GNU/Linux with an NVIDIA GPU of compute capability 3.0+; ARCH in the Makefile defaults to 70 (Volta) and must be edited per GPU
integration.thread_safety: not documented; decode() launches on the default stream and reuses a caller-supplied CUHDGPUDecoderMemory, so concurrent decodes need separate buffers and serialize on the default stream

gotchas: Build is configured by hand-editing CUDA_INCLUDE, CUDA_LIB and ARCH in the Makefile (defaults point at /usr/local/cuda-9.1 and sm_70); there is no CMake or install target.
The caller must know the exact uncompressed size up front to size CUHDOutputBuffer; the stream carries no length or table header.

Auxiliary memory scales with input: one uint4 sync point (16 bytes) plus a 32-bit output count per subsequence, which is 16 bytes of input in the demo configuration (SUBSEQ_SIZE 4, 128 threads), so aux memory is roughly the size of the compressed input.
The repository has no benchmark results; the demo only prints per-phase microsecond timings and checks the round trip on random binomially distributed bytes.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over Huffman_coding_Gap_arrays when the stream format cannot carry a gap array, but prefer the optimized self-sync and gap-array variants in ipdps22-opthuffdec, which report faster decoding with CUHD as their baseline. For CPU decoding of standard Huffman, PIVCO-Huffman or FSE's Huff0 are the practical choices; for GPU entropy decoding with a newer design, the same author's multians (tANS) is the sibling.
verified_claims_summary: Per WebSearch summaries of the peer-reviewed ICPP 2018 paper (not opened; ACM blocked here), GPU decoding on TITAN V, TITAN Xp and GTX 1080 was over an order of magnitude faster than Zstandard's CPU Huffman decoder, and one citing-work snippet puts CUHD at about 10 GB/s; no CPU model, compiler flags or dataset are known, and the comparison pits a GPU against a CPU.
status_note: Abandoned since 2019-02-02 (8 commits, 50 stars, no issues filed); LGPL-3.0, so static linking into closed-source code carries relinking obligations, and the code targets CUDA 8/9-era toolchains.
